items.title: Book Publishers Are Quietly Using More AI. Staff Are Revolting
items.excerpt: Workers at three major publishing houses tell WIRED that LLMs are being used for publicity, cover art, back cover copy and emails, as some execs push junior staff to champion the tech. (Broader multi-house angle beyond the S&S Skan letter published 10-08.)

items.title: Ghostwriters haunted by AI as commissions fall and machine-written manuscripts rise
items.excerpt: Ghostwriters tell The Bookseller that commissions are falling as prospective authors experiment with generative AI, while others are increasingly asked to rework AI-generated manuscripts.

items.title: Frankfurt Book Fair 2026: English language exports, AI and travel chaos lead conversations
items.excerpt: Late-fair wrap: English-language exports, the industry-wide impact of AI, 'travel chaos' missed meetings and the new hall configuration were the most hotly debated topics at this year's Frankfurt Book Fair.

items.title: An editor's first read must not be outsourced to AI
items.excerpt: Comment: used too early in the editorial workflow, AI can suppress an editor's vital but indefinable first-read instincts, argues copy editor Adnan Algin.

items.title: Frankfurt Book Fair 2026: Audible Wants to Turn Every Book into an Audiobook
items.excerpt: Audible CCO Rachel Ghiazza says the company expects to use AI tools across the entire audiobook production process to reach 'every book in every language', and will launch in Indonesia, South Korea, Denmark, Norway and Finland in 2027.

items.title: Frankfurt Book Fair 2026: Publishing Jobs Will Adapt to AI, Not Disappear
items.excerpt: Bloomsbury founder Nigel Newton called the idea that AI will take all publishing jobs 'rubbish', but panelists agreed entry-level roles may vanish, staff need retraining and new roles will emerge.

items.title: Frankfurt Book Fair 2026: Three Views of Innovation
items.excerpt: The CEOs of Sourcebooks, Abrams and Perfect Bound on implementing AI in legacy publishing: Stable and Perfect Bound have adopted AI across accounting, marketing and production, with one CEO calling AI 'the worst thing that has happened to humanity' yet necessary to compete.

items.title: Frankfurter Buchmesse 2026: EU AI Act Gives Publishers Leverage, but No Teeth
items.excerpt: Specialists at Frankfurter Buchmesse said the EU's AI rules help rights holders on paper yet lack penalties for AI developers and incentives for researchers.

items.title: Frankfurter Buchmesse 2026: Audible-Commissioned Survey Finds Audio Sends Readers Back to Print; Half Would Try AI Narration
items.excerpt: An Audible survey by NielsenIQ across 11 markets finds audiobooks pull listeners toward print and e-books, and half of respondents are open to AI-narrated content (42% Germany to 66% Japan). Same Audible presser as PW 101500.

items.title: Frankfurter Buchmesse 2026: Tonies Bets On a Kids' Audio Future that Is Screenless, Serialized, with Content (Often) Made In-house
items.excerpt: Tonies trialed an AI 'storyteller' with 3,000 households generating personalized children's stories, and 85% of staff use AI daily, but CEO Tobias Wann insists the Toniebox 'will never become an AI toy'.

items.title: Datenturbo: KI für Metadaten
items.excerpt: Berlin start-up Snackz turns book-trade requirements into an AI offering for publishers and retailers, from metadata management to an online-shop chatbot.

items.title: Neues Label: "Von Menschen gemacht"
items.excerpt: 18 German-language children's and YA publishers launch a 'Von Menschen - geschrieben - gestaltet - geprüft' label certifying that text, illustration and design are human-made and editorially checked. (Distinct from UK Books By People mark.)

items.title: Frankfurter Buchmesse 2026: Report after two days of the fair
items.excerpt: Official interim report: 65,000 trade visitors from 130 countries, new hall layout, and 'AI dominates the conversation' across CEO talks (Tonies, Bloomsbury) and the opening event. Date from release URL slug; no og:image.

items.title: From Story Seeds To Stories, And Writing An Author's Note, With Joanna Penn
items.excerpt: Joanna Penn on turning story ideas into fiction and why an author's note matters more in an age of AI (podcast episode).

items.title: Audible will launch in new countries in 2027
items.excerpt: Audible will launch localized listener experiences in Indonesia, South Korea, Denmark, Norway and Finland next year. Duplicate of PW 101500 Audible story; alternate only.

items.title: How to Listen to Kindle Books With CastReader
items.excerpt: Guide to CastReader, which reads Kindle books aloud with cloud AI voices and an 'AI Explain' feature. Low priority: how-to, possibly sponsored.
